PullRequest.Title: refactor: edit operations timeline
PullRequest.Body:
Previously, the timeline of edit operations worked by simply taking a snapshot of the working set at each request and undo stop. This has a few downsides. It was inefficient, especially for large files, and we only saw a capture of resources states and not what changed between them. For this reason, operations like file deletions, renames, and (to a lesser extent) file creations could not be represented.

This PR replaces that with an operation-based log. This is a 'lossless' log which lets us undo and redo operations more correctly, representing other types of operations. We also only take a snapshot of files that get edited once per request, and rebuild intermediate content by replaying edits to the text/notebook models. It is more expressive, better tested, and gives us more extensibility as we start looking into other edit models (e.g. external snapshots that comes through ACP.)

Users should see pretty much no difference in the new model aside from the fact that this fixes #253521, fixes #250507 and fixes #261032.

Seeking approval on this today but I'm going to continue selfhosting this for another half day before merging

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The branch truncation path, full-content baseline ownership, absence of any deletion path, and unconditional persistence of the map are all directly traced. Only the exact file sizes and number of user branches vary.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Full text contents and serialized notebook snapshots retained in `_fileBaselines`, plus the same bytes embedded in persisted timeline JSON
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each undo-then-new-request branch can retain another full baseline per edited file; retained memory and saved `state.json` bytes grow with the sum of file sizes across abandoned requests rather than the reachable timeline.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Retained memory, larger JSON serialization/allocation, and increasing save/shutdown filesystem I/O
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The deleted `pushSnapshot` branch logic rebuilt `newLinearHistory` only through the current pointer, so snapshots from the abandoned future branch became unreachable and were not persisted.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new branch path truncates `_operations` and filters `_checkpoints`, but leaves every baseline in `_fileBaselines`; `getStateForPersistence` later returns the entire map.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 240 explicitly drops future operations on branching, and the adjacent added branch-truncation block drops future checkpoints without deleting their request/file baselines; this creates stale retained state that the previous history truncation released.
Findings.Title: Prune baselines when truncating a branch
Findings.Impact: A user who repeatedly undoes an agent request and sends an alternative request against large files accumulates unreachable full-file baselines for the lifetime of the chat session, and every state save writes those stale contents into `state.json`.
Findings.Evidence: `recordFileOperation` truncates operations at line 240 and checkpoints immediately afterward, while repository-wide uses of `_fileBaselines` show insertion, lookup, persistence, and restore only—no branch cleanup. Each `IFileBaseline.content` is a full text or serialized notebook snapshot, and `ChatEditingSessionStorage.storeState` assigns `timeline` directly before `JSON.stringify(data)`.
Findings.Recommendation: When truncating a branch, remove baselines that are no longer reachable from the surviving operations/checkpoints, while preserving the newly recorded request baseline, and persist only that pruned set.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The undo/redo call path and one-model-per-operation loop are explicit, and streamed response updates demonstrably create separate operations. Only the typical batch count and file size affect severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Temporary TextModel instances, full-file text buffers/strings, and CPU work to rebuild them
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N recorded edit batches to an S-byte file, replay constructs and disposes N text models and materializes a full string after every batch, making reconstruction roughly O(N × S) allocation/work instead of applying N batches to one model and reading once.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased undo/redo and historical-diff latency with heavy CPU and GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Undo restored the selected snapshot's already-materialized content once per file; it did not recreate a full text model for every streamed edit batch during the undo action.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The operation-log replay loop invokes `_applyTextEditsToContent` for each `TextEdit` operation, and this added line constructs a fresh TextModel from the entire intermediate content each time.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 650 creates the per-operation temporary TextModel inside `_applyTextEditsToContent`, which is called from the newly added replay loop once for every recorded text operation.
Findings.Title: Replay text edits in one temporary model
Findings.Impact: Undoing or opening a historical diff after an agent produced many incremental edits in a large file can synchronously allocate and rebuild that file dozens or hundreds of times before the action completes.
Findings.Evidence: Each response update is recorded as a separate `TextEdit` operation in `ChatEditingSession._recordEditOperations`. `_navigateToEpoch` awaits reconstruction on undo/redo; `_replayOperations` loops those operations, and every text operation reaches lines 647-669, creating a TextModel, applying one batch, calling `getValue`, and disposing it.
Findings.Recommendation: Create one temporary model per text-file replay, apply all chronological text-operation batches to it (resetting only across create/delete boundaries), then materialize the final string once.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The operation-per-stream-update call path, global listener fan-out, replay, model-change signal, and worker diff are explicit. Debouncing reduces frequency for tightly packed batches, so exact magnitude depends on stream cadence and visible pill count, not on the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread operation-log scans, temporary text models/full strings, model updates, and editor-worker diff IPC/CPU
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each visible collapsed code-block model subscribes to the global operation list. After each 500 ms quiet interval, every subscriber replays its file's growing operation prefix; for B spaced edit batches this can sum to O(B² × file size), multiplied by visible pills, even when an operation belongs to another URI.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Sustained CPU/GC and editor-worker load during agent streaming, causing slower edit application and UI responsiveness on large or multi-file responses
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The old timeline updated a stop snapshot when a streaming edit group resolved and diffed those stable snapshots; it did not rebuild a live end-state model from every recorded edit batch.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every operation now invalidates a global listener per dynamic snapshot; each listener calls `getContentAtStop`, updates its model, and the model change launches another advanced worker diff.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 320 newly connects every operation-list mutation to every live snapshot model; this moves reconstruction and worker diffing onto the streaming path and increases both frequency and cross-file fan-out versus completion-only snapshots.
Findings.Title: Avoid replaying every pill for each streamed operation
Findings.Impact: While an agent streams edits into large files—especially several files with visible collapsed pills—ordinary edit batches can repeatedly reconstruct full contents and run up-to-3-second diffs before the response is complete.
Findings.Evidence: `_acceptEdits` records one operation for each newly streamed edit batch. Added line 320 listens to the unfiltered global `_operations`; line 326 calls `getContentAtStop`, which scans/filter-sorts the log and replays all matching operations. `getSnapshotModel` then calls `model.setValue`, and `_getEntryDiffBetweenEpochs` observes that change and invokes `computeDiff(... maxComputationTimeMs: 3000)`. `ThrottledDelayer` serializes per pill but does not coalesce across pills.
Findings.Recommendation: Filter updates by affected URI and avoid recomputing the full diff until the edit group/checkpoint is final; if live counts are required, maintain an incrementally updated per-file reconstruction and coalesce/cancel worker diffs across pills.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: At each new chat request, the old `createSnapshot` path synchronously iterated the complete editing working set and materialized a full snapshot of every entry, including full text/notebook contents.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Starting requests with an existing large edited working set incurred collection-wide copying/allocation and retained repeated full snapshots in timeline history.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added line records only lightweight checkpoint metadata; full baselines are now captured only for files actually edited in that request, once per file/request.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: `installAutoApplyObserver` calls `session.createSnapshot` for every added request. In the base revision, line 230 selects `_createSnapshot`, whose deleted implementation loops all `_entriesObs` and calls each entry's full `createSnapshot`. Added line 257 replaces this with `createCheckpoint`; `_acceptStreamingEditsStart` lazily records one baseline only for the touched resource. `blame_base_line` resolves the old mechanism to the supplied commit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent streams text or notebook edits while collapsed code-block pills are rendered
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Per-resource edit application is sequenced and remains the direct streaming critical path. The new snapshot refresh runs after a 500 ms debounce, but reconstructs models on the UI side and then consumes the shared editor worker, so it competes with continued editing even when not directly awaited by `pushText`.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize the changed snapshot models and compute an advanced text diff in the editor worker
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial request per pill, then another after each debounced model update; aggregate scales with visible pills, including pills unrelated to the changed URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Stable stop snapshots were updated when a streaming edit group resolved; operation-by-operation dynamic end models and their global invalidation did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous to the immediate edit callback but consumes the shared worker and follows main-thread reconstruction/model updates, degrading streaming responsiveness.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the number of newly observed edit batches B, matching operations in the file/history, and visible pills V. Rapid updates coalesce per pill, but spaced updates replay a growing prefix; every pill listens to the global operation list, including operations for other files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Edits are serialized per resource by `SequencerByKey` and throttled to at least 15 ms. Each pill has its own `ThrottledDelayer`, which prevents overlap for that pill, but there is no URI filtering or shared limiter across pills; worker diff requests can queue across V pills.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Text model references are reused for a snapshot URI while alive, but reconstructed content has no per-file/per-epoch cache. Each invalidation scans and replays the log from the baseline, and diff observables/results are not shared across pills.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: operation recording, global invalidation, full replay, model update, and worker diff are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact cost depends on edit cadence, file size, and how many pills remain rendered; tightly packed updates are debounced. The full replay and cross-file fan-out are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression: global operation changes repeatedly reconstruct and diff live pill models.

Scenarios.Scenario: User invokes chat-edit undo, redo, or opens a historical diff after many incremental edits
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Checkpoint navigation awaits structural operations, reconstruction of every affected file, and `setContents`; historical model creation also awaits reconstruction before the diff can render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create, delete, or rename resources through `IBulkEditService` while crossing structural operations
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One boundary action per create/delete/rename operation in the traversed epoch range, serialized in order.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Snapshot restore set each recorded entry's state and did not replay a structural operation log; create/delete/rename representation was absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly awaited before reconstruction and completion of undo/redo.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute diffs for reconstructed historical text models in the editor worker
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per observed historical diff pair after its two models are reconstructed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous timeline also used the editor worker for stable snapshot diffs, but without operation replay to obtain model contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The historical diff UI waits for the result; undo/redo itself does not await this worker call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of affected files F, total operations E, edit batches N per file, and file/notebook size S. Effective text replay cost is N full temporary-model builds for each file; log filtering also scans E for each reconstructed file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Structural filesystem operations are awaited serially in epoch order. File reconstructions then launch with `Promise.all` across affected URIs; operations within each replay are sequential, with no shared limiter across files.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No reconstructed checkpoint cache is used. Every navigation or model request starts from a baseline and replays matching operations; warm model references help only after that particular snapshot URI remains alive.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: navigation awaits `_reconstructAllFileContents`, `_replayOperations` loops batches, and each text operation constructs/disposes a full TextModel.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number and size of agent edit batches vary, but a text edit group is explicitly updated multiple times during streaming, so multi-operation replay is normal rather than hypothetical.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable latency regression: one temporary full-file model is created per edit batch instead of once per reconstructed file.

Scenarios.Scenario: User undoes requests and submits alternative requests, then the global editing session is saved or shut down
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Branch creation itself mutates in-memory history synchronously. Saving captures the full timeline, JSON-stringifies it, and awaits a filesystem write; shutdown joins an outstanding storage task.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write JSON session state containing all timeline baselines
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One state-file write per session/save event; bytes include every retained baseline, including abandoned branches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Future snapshot branches were removed from `newLinearHistory`, and snapshot contents were hash-deduplicated into content files rather than keeping abandoned baselines in persisted state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Normally asynchronous to editing, but session stop awaits it and shutdown joins an outstanding save.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of abandoned branches A multiplied by edited file/notebook baseline sizes. The effective retained cardinality is one full baseline per URI/request key, including requests whose operations and checkpoints were truncated.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A session save is one filesystem write after serialization; saves for global sessions are launched together with `Promise.all`, while repeated save events are chained through `storageTask`.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Initial/recent snapshot content uses hash-based deduplication in the contents folder, but timeline baselines bypass that cache and are embedded directly in `state.json`. No pruning occurs when a future branch is discarded.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: only operations/checkpoints are truncated, the baseline map has no deletion path, and all entries are persisted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Impact depends on how often users branch and on file sizes; repeated regenerate/undo workflows and large generated files make growth realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable unbounded-retention regression affecting memory and save/shutdown I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: A new request starts in an existing large chat editing working set
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The add-request observer synchronously calls `session.createSnapshot` before observing response edits. After this change that call creates lightweight checkpoint metadata; a full baseline is deferred until a file is actually edited.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Previously all F existing entries and their content sizes were copied per request; now baseline work scales only with files touched by the request and occurs once per URI/request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous checkpoint creation; per-file baseline creation is serialized with the resource's streaming-edit start.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `hasFileBaseline` provides one baseline per URI/request. There is no extra boundary call for untouched entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the add-request call path and deleted full-entry loop are explicit, and blame identified the introducing commit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact prior delay depended on working-set and notebook sizes, but the removed collection-wide full snapshot mechanism is direct.
Scenarios.Verdict: This PR fixes a concrete serialization/allocation regression; recorded internally with `report_regression_fix`, not as a review finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 29 changed files and relevant call paths. Submitted three findings: stale full baselines survive branch truncation, live pills fan out replay/diff work from every operation, and text replay rebuilds a full temporary model per edit batch. Also recorded the verified removal of request-start whole-working-set snapshots as a regression fix.
